messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER: control-plane authz/gateway 5xx spike detected — paging SRE. incident_id=INC-2945678 :rotating_light: See runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/controlplane-deps

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook 'controlplane-deps-5xx' matched. Suggested first steps: 1) assess blast radius, 2) enable fallback auth cache, 3) open circuit on tokenservice. Logs: /logs/INC-2945678

maria: i'm on it. quick check: is this hitting tokenservice or gateway? grafana shows 502 spikes in gateway, but 5xx from /v1/auth/validate upstream return 502/504.

jess: seeing same. customer-facing error rate at 12% for API keys validation across us-east-1. top affected paths: /v1/auth/validate, /v1/org/lookup.

nora: thrown alarms: controlplane latency svc: authz.tokenservice p50 -> 400ms, p95 -> 2.3s, error rate -> 18% in last 5m.

tony: I can take the live debug if you need me to run failover. handing off in 10 if no blockers.

maria: quick impact assessment — internal metric: approx 1800 user requests affected/minute, likely causing downstream 502 to hosted customers for short calls. no broad DB errors. billing and config checks look normal.

jess: i deployed a canary config 09:12 UTC, could be related. can anyone check rollout list? `kubectl -n controlplane rollout status deploy/authz --watch`

infra-bot: rollout history for deploy/authz: revision 42 (09:11 UTC) started by jess. previous stable revision 41.

maria: pausing rollout now: `kubectl -n controlplane rollout undo deploy/authz --to-revision=41`

(5s later)
maria: undo executed, pods rolling back. accepting increased error transient as pods cycle.

jess: confirming rollback started. watching metrics.

nora: after rollback, error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in 60s. p95 latency reduced to 540ms. looks like the canary was the regression.

tonY: (typo) sorry — updated: tony: good catch. we should pin canary until we reproduce.

maria: opening a short mitigation task: enable auth cache fallback to reduce calls to tokenservice. command: `kubectl -n controlplane set env deploy/authz AUTH_CACHE_MODE=fallback`

infra-bot: env update applied to deploy/authz, new pods started.

jess: rolling back canary also prevents new config-changes from entering. normalizing traffic.

maria: customer impact note for ops: A subset of API keys saw 502/504 from auth validation between 09:11-09:16 UTC. Estimated affected requests ~9k. No customer data exposure. Recommend status page: "Intermittent authentication errors for API requests in US-EAST between 09:11-09:16 UTC; mitigation applied."

nora: can someone capture stack traces from tokenservice for the failing requests? `kubectl logs deploy/tokenservice -n controlplane --since=10m | grep "ERROR" | head -n50`

jess: grabbing logs, posting snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z ERROR tokenservice validate request failed status=502 internal=timeout reading upstream auth-db
2026-03-15T09:12:04Z WARN retrying request id=3f2b... reason=upstream_timeout
```

maria: looks like the canary changed timeout/keepalive behavior to upstream auth-db. That caused more connection churn and timeouts.

tonY: (again corrected) tony: i'll run a canary test locally with the change to reproduce. also i'll own the incident postmortem. handing off live pager to tony now :phone: @tony oncall

maria: handing off to @tony for night coverage. all immediate mitigations applied: rollback canary, enable cache fallback. monitoring at normalizing. please escalate if error rate >10% again.

tony: taking over. quick checklist: 1) validate rollback fully completed 2) confirm fallback cache TTL 3) schedule revert if stable.

nora: creating incident ticket INC-2945678 with summary and timeline. linking to PR #4421 and rollout rev 42. will add logs and graphs.

maria: adding follow-up action: reproduce locally, add e2e that simulates upstream timeouts, and add circuit-breaker test. assign to jess.

jess: ack, will create PR to tighten upstream keepalive and add e2e.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2945678 marked 'mitigated' by maria at 09:22 UTC. No further paging for this incident. :white_check_mark:
